rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines imlāl as dictating from memory and infers that the debtor should propose and dictate the written debt record.
rows.anchor: İmlâl; “imlâ” kelimesinin aslı veya mürâdifidir ki ezbere söyleyip yazdırmak demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While dictating, the debtor must fear God rather than the scribe and must not reduce any part of the creditor’s right.
rows.anchor: borçlu taraf teklif etmeli, o yazdırmalıdır. Binâen‘aleyh tamamen imlâ etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must not use deception or insert defensive clauses that alter the legal course of the transaction now or later.
rows.anchor: ifadesinde hîle ve hud‘aya saparak veya bazı kuyûd-ı müdâfi‘a derc ederek vak‘anın hâlen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debtor unable to dictate includes a spendthrift fool, a minor or mentally deficient person, or anyone unable because of muteness, stammering, ignorance, or another cause.
rows.anchor: malını israf ve telef eder hafif akıllı bir sefih yahut sagīr veya ma‘tuh bir zaîf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor’s guardian, trustee, agent, translator, or the creditor as debt-holder may dictate in the debtor’s place, fairly and justly.
rows.anchor: velîsi, yani onun yerine işine bakan veliyy-i umûru, vasîsi, vekîli, tercümanı yahut veliyy-i deyn olan dâin adl ü hakkāniyet vechile imlâ etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “your men” excludes children and non-Muslim men’s testimony against Muslims as sufficient testimony.
rows.anchor: مِنَ الرِّجَالِ buyurulmayıp da مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ buyurulması çocukların

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses must be people whose testimony is accepted and whose justice and reliability are known; a random pairing is not valid.
rows.anchor: şehadetlerine râzı olacağınız, sizce adalet ve mevsûkiyetleri mâlum şâhidlerden bulunsunlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice is also required by the instruction in 65:2 to appoint two just witnesses from among you.
rows.anchor: buyurulduğu gibi adalet de şarttır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Hamza’s reading, if one woman forgets or errs, the other reminds her.
rows.anchor: yahut –Hamza kıraatine göre– birisi unutur, şaşırırsa birisi diğerine hatırlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness competence requires sound retention; witnesses lacking moral probity or reliable acquisition or retention of evidence are not admissible.
rows.anchor: şehâdete ehliyetin şartlarından birisi de hakkıyla zapt u hıfzdır. Ahlâk-ı marziyyesi olmayanların şehâdeti muteber olmayacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A witness need not remember the event continuously, provided they can properly recall it when giving testimony.
rows.anchor: Fakat zabt için evvelinden âhirine kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who recorded an event, later forgot it, and then recalls it clearly by consulting the record may testify.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bir vakayı defterine kaydeden bunu bir müddet unutsa da sonra o deftere müracaat ettiği zaman zihninden iyice hatırlarsa şehadet edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who only knows they made a record but still cannot recall the event must not testify.
rows.anchor: Kendi kendine “kaydetmişim, amma hâlâ iyi hatırlayamıyorum” diyorsa edemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses should not be prompted; one who has forgotten should be able to remember independently.
rows.anchor: Şâhidlerin ihtâra tâbi‘olması da iyi olmaz, unutan şâhid kendiliğinden hatırlayabilmeli.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requiring at least two witnesses removes suspicion and the possibility of error or forgetfulness, displaying the strength of their retention and justice.
rows.anchor: Nisâb-ı şehâdetin lâekal iki olması da reyb ü töhmeti, ihtimâl-i hatâ ve nisyânı bertaraf ederek zabtın ve adâletin kuvvetini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He generalizes that women’s retention is weaker and forgetfulness more likely than men’s, while allowing individual exceptions and treating gender and the majority as the legal reference.
rows.anchor: İşte sûret-i umûmiyede mülâhaza edildiği zaman erkeklere nisbetle kadınlarda kuvvet-i zabt nâkıs ve ihtimâl-i nisyan gālibdir. Böyle olmayanları bulunabilirse de itibar cinse ve ekseredir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attributes women’s alleged forgetfulness partly to greater sensitivity and emotional impressions, which can weaken recall even in intelligent people.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ kadınlık fıtratında hassâsiyet gālibdir ve galebe-i hassâsiyet, kesret-i teessürâtı istilzam eder. Kesret-i teessür ise esbâb-ı nisyandandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says women are more inwardly oriented and less engaged with external affairs such as commerce and debts, which he regards as primarily men’s work.
rows.anchor: Hâdisât-ı âfâkiye onu derece-i sâniyede alâkadar eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says modesty and reserve predominate in women and should do so, and that even a small engagement diminishes their distinct worth and leaves fewer reminders of events.
rows.anchor: Sâlisen kadında hayâ ve hicab gālibdir ve gālib olmalıdır. Onun kıymet-i nev‘iyyesi en cüz’î bir meşgūliyetle zâyi‘olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls a woman’s becoming manlike a degradation and says both feminized men’s and masculinized women’s testimony is inadmissible because they depart from their sex-specific perfection and may distort truth.
rows.anchor: erkekleşmek kadın için bir züldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats women’s comparatively lower retention of external events as a consequence of their sex-specific nature, while saying a woman who later recalls an event fully can testify.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde fıtrat-ı hak kadının kemâliyle erkeğin kemâlini bi’l-vücûh tefrik etmiş bulunduğundan kadının vâkı‘ât-ı hâriciyeye ait zabtında noksan ihtimâli fazla bulunması kemâl-i nev‘îsinin muktezâsıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unjust to compel women to record events or, after a human lapse of memory, to make them recover recollection through outside prompts.
rows.anchor: Kadını re’sen zabt-ı vâkı‘aya mecbur tutmak revâ-yı hak olmadığı gibi lede’l-îcâb üzerine tahmil edilen şehâdeti de hasbe’l-beşeriyye unuttuğu zaman da onu hâricî muhtıralarla tahattura sevketmek de revâ-yı hak değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two women can confer before testifying and remind one another without outside prompting, strengthening their recall and preserving both their dignity and the right entrusted to them.
rows.anchor: bunlar edâ-yı şehâdetten evvel hâricî hiçbir ihtâra tâbi‘ve muhtaç olmaksızın yekdiğeriyle hasbihâl ederek kendi kendilerine mütekābil ihtârât ile zabtlarını takviye ve tesbit edebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If neither woman forgot, their evidentiary position is stronger; the mutual reminder need not happen in court, where it could prevent acceptance of testimony.
rows.anchor: Şayet hiç unutmamış bulunurlarsa vaziyetleri daha kuvvetli olur. Şu hâlde bu tezkîr ü ihtar mahkemede edâ-yı şehâdet sırasında olacak diye anlaşılmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where men can know the matter, women should not be made witnesses; if no man is available and a woman must be called, two women should serve for one man.
rows.anchor: umûrda kadın işhâd edilmemeli, kadınlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For matters men cannot witness, women’s reports alone may suffice, sometimes even one woman’s report, as with an incident in a women’s bath or a midwife’s report of birth.
rows.anchor: erkeklerin muttali‘olmaları câiz olmayan husûsâtta yalnız kadınların ihbârıyla ve hatta sırasına göre bir kadının ihbârıyla da amel câiz olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A summons to bear or give testimony must not be refused: testimony is a collective duty, and becomes individually obligatory when nobody else can meet the need or particular people are required.
rows.anchor: gerek tahammül ve gerek edâ olsun, şehadet için vukū‘bulan davete icâbet farz-ı kifâyedir. Hiç kimse gitmezse herkes âsim olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars restrict the prohibition to accepting testimony, others to giving it, and many choose the latter; the author follows the view that the wording is unrestricted and includes both.
rows.anchor: Bazı ulemâ bu nehyin yalnız tahammüle, bazıları da yalnız edâya ait olduğunu beyan etmişler ve birçokları ikinciye hükmeylemişler ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatada relates that the verse was revealed after a man went from camp to camp seeking a witness and no one paid attention.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den “bu hususta bir adam oba oba dolaşır kimse aldırmazdı, bu nâzil oldu” diye rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although giving testimony is especially important, necessity can make both accepting and giving testimony individually obligatory.
rows.anchor: edâ farîzası daha mühim olmakla beraber ihtiyaç vukû‘unda gerek tahammül ve gerek edâ-yı şehâdet farz-ı ‘ayn olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every debt, large or small, should be documented in detail through its due date, including all particulars and qualities, rather than dismissed as too minor to write.
rows.anchor: büyük olsun küçük olsun o deyni veya hakkı eceline varıncaya kadar yazmaktan usanmayınız, az olsun çok olsun yazınız ve ecel ü müddetine varıncaya kadar bütün müfredât ve evsâfıyla mufassalan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the command to keep writing as an explanation and emphasis of the earlier command, directed to scribes; the author finds the broader contextual reading more fitting.
rows.anchor: Bu fıkra bâlâdaki فَٱكْتُبُوهُ emrinin bir tavzih ve te’kîdi olmak üzere kâtiblere hitab gibi tefsir olunuyor. Fakat bunun daha şümullü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers understanding the command to address both parties, scribes, and witnesses, urging them to keep their own records and, where possible, write down testimony they have undertaken.
rows.anchor: gerek dâyin ve gerek medyun tarafından deynin ayrıca kendi defterlerine kaydını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Detailed documentation has three benefits: it is most just before God, supports the establishment of testimony, and most nearly prevents doubt.
rows.anchor: Allah ‘indinde a‘deldir, en ziyade adl ü istikāmettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A complete record secures confidence about the debt’s kind, amount, term, witnesses, testimony, and the parties’ moral, legal, and social relations.
rows.anchor: cinsinde, mikdârında, müddetinde, şâhidinde, şehâdetinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is a fully cash, hand-to-hand commercial transaction; in that case leaving it unwritten causes no blame.
rows.anchor: meğer ki yaptığınız iş aranızda yed-be-yed alıp vereceğiniz tamamen peşin hâzır bir ticaret muâmelesi olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a cash sale may be written privately or in a short memorandum, though the burden on people who cannot write may outweigh the benefit.
rows.anchor: her ihtimâle karşı husûsî bir surette veya icmâlen yekdiğerine bir muhtıra olmak üzere mümkin olduğu kadar yazılıverirse fena da olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For any sale, including a cash sale, make it openly in the presence of witnesses rather than secretly; this precaution protects property and legal security.
rows.anchor: velev peşin olsun bir mübâya‘a, bir alım satım yaptığınızda işhâd ediniz, şâhid huzurunda alenen yapınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes regard witnessing a sale here as a recommendation for precaution.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn beyan ediyorlar ki bu âyetteki nedb ihtiyat içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to harm a scribe or witness can mean they must not harm rights-holders by refusing a request or falsifying or altering the writing or testimony.
rows.anchor: ‘inde’l-mürâca‘a icâbet etmemek veya kitâbet ü şehâdeti tahrif ve tağyir eylemek gibi ahlâksızlıkla ashâb-ı hukūku zararlandırmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, on the passive reading, scribes and witnesses themselves must not be harmed by excessive demands, interruption of important work, or denial of a scribe’s fee.
rows.anchor: ne kâtib, ne şâhid ızrar edilmesin, bunlara kitabet veya şehadet gibi bir vazîfe-i dîniye tahmil olunurken kendilerince mühim olan işlerinden alıkonulmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causing such harm is a transgression against God’s obedience.
rows.anchor: bu her hâlde sizin için bir fısktır,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will teach people more knowledge and rulings that serve their welfare.
rows.anchor: Allah size daha ziyade ilimler öğretecek, mesâlihinizi tazammun eden ahkâmını, ma‘ârifini belletecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God knows everything, believers should obey commands, avoid prohibitions, trust His promise, honor Him, and secure their dealings; piety is the foundation of that security.
rows.anchor: tevsik din ve takva olduğunu unutmayınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge is the recourse when traveling and no scribe is available, but these conditions concern resort to collateral, not its validity or permissibility.
rows.anchor: bu şartlar rehnin sıhhat ve cevâzının değil, tevsik için ta‘ayyününün şartıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s travel-and-no-scribe condition cannot be inverted to forbid pledges when one is resident or a scribe is available; the lack of a scribe makes writing impossible.
rows.anchor: bu şartın “seferde olmaz veya kâtib bulursanız rehin alamazsınız” diye mefhûm-ı muhâlifi muteber değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel is the customary or usual cause of lacking a scribe, not a restrictive condition; the same rule applies to another excuse that prevents finding a scribe while resident.
rows.anchor: Sefer bunun sebeb-i âdî ve ekserîsidir. Ta‘bîr-i âharla ihtirâzî değil, kayd-ı vukū‘îdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge is permissible while resident too, as shown by the Prophet pledging his coat of mail in a settled state.
rows.anchor: Hazarda rehnin cevâzı fi‘l-i nebevî ile de sâbittir. Çünkü Resûlullah hâl-i hazarda zırhlı gömleğini rehnetmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When writing can secure a debt, requesting a pledge between believers is permissible but not recommended unless there is an excuse.
rows.anchor: senet ve kitabet ile tevsik mümkin oldukça mü’minler beynindeki müdâyenâtta rehin talep etmek câiz olsa da mendub olmayacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking possession is required to complete a pledge; an unpossessed pledge gives no security, and an undivided fractional share cannot properly be pledged.
rows.anchor: rehnin tamam olması için kabz şarttır, makbuz olmayan rehin bir tevsik ifade etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing, witnessing, and pledging are the three means of securing debts and transactions; faith and piety should encourage these protections of people’s rights and lawful wealth.
rows.anchor: müdâyenât ve mu‘âmelâtta üç nevi tevsik vardır: Kitabet, işhâd, rehin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Securing lawful wealth enables lawful earning and spending in God’s path and helps avoid usury and similar sins so that piety can continue.
rows.anchor: mâl-i helâli muhafaza ve helâk ü zayâ‘dan sıyânet ederek tarîk-i meşrû‘ile kesb ü istihsâle sa‘y eylemelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest assurance for human rights is obedience to God through faith and piety; without it, secondary safeguards have limited benefit.
rows.anchor: hukūk-ı beşer için bu meyanda en büyük te’mînât Hak teâlâ’ya inkıyad ile ahkâmına i‘tisâm bahş eden hiss-i dîn ü takvâdadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is permissible for parties to dispense with all three securities and rely wholly on mutual trust; the trusted debtor must repay the trust.
rows.anchor: bazınız bazınıza, bazı dâyinler bazı medyunlara tamamen emniyet eder, rehin almaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission to rely on trust shows that writing, witnessing, and pledging are recommendations rather than obligations; otherwise this permission would abrogate the prior commands.
rows.anchor: vücûb için değil, nedb içindir.

rows.speaker: Hasan, Şa‘bî, Hakem b. Uteybe
rows.claim: Hasan, al-Shaʿbi, and al-Hakam b. Utayba are among exegetes who say this verse abrogates the earlier instructions.
rows.anchor: mahmul olursa o vücûbun bununla mensuh olmasını iktizâ edecektir. Fi’l-hakīka Hasan, Şa‘bî,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly says the debt verse is not abrogated but remains decisive; with no proof that this verse came later, most exegetes agree there is no abrogation.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretleri âyet-i müdâyenede nesih yoktur, muhkemdir diye tasrih ettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes treat permission to rely on trust as evidence that the securities are recommended; ʿAta, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Nakhaʿi instead make the pledge recommended while treating feasible writing and witnessing as obligatory.
rows.anchor: ekserîsi işbu cevâz-ı emniyetin nâsih değil, karîne-i nedb olduğuna; Atâ, İbn Cüreyc, Nehaî gibi bazıları da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi’s account in Ahkam al-Qur’an says the juristic position is recommendation.
rows.anchor: Ahkâm-ı Kur’ân’da Ebû Bekir Râzî’nin beyânına nazaran fıkıh nedb üzerindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the status of the safeguards, the person entrusted with property is obligated to discharge the trust fully and must fear God rather than misuse the trust.
rows.anchor: emniyet edilen şahıs emaneti bihakkın edâ etmek farz olduğunu bilsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must neither refuse to testify when needed nor conceal known truth; debtors likewise must not deny a debt they know and have witnessed.
rows.anchor: ey şâhidler lede’l-hâce edâ-yı şehadetten hem imtinâ‘etmeyiniz, hem de görüp bildiğiniz hakk u hakikati gizlemeyiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealing testimony is a grave inward sin of the heart, the locus of faith, and approaches unbelief or lack of creed.
rows.anchor: Ketm-i şehadet günahı öyle zâhirî ve hâricî bir uzvun günahı değil, bizzat mahall-i iman olan kalb ve nefsin bir günahıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas counts associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest major sins.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir ki “ekber-i kebâir Allah’a şirk, yalancı şâhidlik ve ketm-i şehâdettir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every hidden and manifest act, including giving or concealing testimony, and will punish accordingly.
rows.anchor: Allah ise şehadet veya ketm-i şehadet gibi gizli açık, zâhir veya bâtında her ne yaparsanız tamamıyla bilir. Sırası gelince cezasını verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul means the food, drink, and other hospitality prepared for a guest on arrival; he renders it in Turkish as “konukluk.”
rows.anchor: “Nüzül”; Bir müsâfire ilk geldiği sırada ikram edilmek üzere hazırlanan yiyecek içecek ve sâir ikrâmiye ki Türkçe “konukluk” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some among the disbelievers eventually attain a good end and join the believers; the verse’s final wording indicates people who will become Muslims.
rows.anchor: bunlar cidden Müslüman olacaklardır. Ve nitekim bu âna kadar olagelmişler ve yine olacaklardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion of revelation identifies Jewish Abdullah b. Salam and his companions, or converts from Najran, Abyssinia, and Rome (forty, thirty, and eight) as the people who believed.
rows.anchor: Musevî iken Müslüman olan Abdullah b. Selâm ve arkadaşlarının veya Îsevî iken Müslüman olan ehl-i Necran’dan kırk, Habeş’ten otuz, Rum’dan sekiz

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Câbir, Katâde
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Jabir, and Qatada report that the verse concerned the Negus Ashama: after his death the Prophet prayed over him in absentia, prompting hypocrites to object that he prayed over a Christian he had never seen.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ve Câbir ve Katâde demişlerdir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the Negus report the most widespread and dates Ashama’s death to the ninth year after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: da hicretin dokuzuncu senesinde vukū‘bulmuştur.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about all People of the Book who came to believe.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid buna kāil olmuştur ki mazmûn-ı âyete bu daha muvâfık görülmüştür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the general reading about believing People of the Book because the wording “will believe” appears to refer to the future.
rows.anchor: âyete bu daha muvâfık görülmüştür. Zira لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ her hâlde iman ederler mânasına istikbâlde zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says patience has three degrees: patience in affliction, in obedience, and in avoiding sin.
rows.anchor: Haberde vârid olduğuna göre sabır üç derecedir: Musibete sabır, tâatte sabır, masiyetten sabır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should outdo God’s enemies in patience at trials and struggle, and strive to overcome their own lower desires.
rows.anchor: sabırda Allah düşmanlarıyla yarışıp onların üstüne çıkınız, yani imtihan ve mücahede mevki‘lerinde düşmanların sabrının fevkine çıkmaya ve hevâ-yı nefsinizi yenmeye çalışınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat means maintaining mutual attachment to duty, like congregational prayer behind an imam, and especially preparing for war and guarding the borders with horses tethered.
rows.anchor: Ve murâbata ediniz, ribat yapınız, imam ardında cemaatle namaz gibi birbirinize bağlanıp vazifeye mukayyed olunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat originally means binding horses to watch and await an enemy; the term later covers mounted or foot soldiers posted at Islamic border stations.
rows.anchor: “Ribat”; Allah yolunda mülâzemettir. Bu esasen “rabt-ı hayl” yani at bağlamaktan me’huzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In juristic usage a murabit goes to a border station to wait for a period; local residents who live there with their families and earn a livelihood are not called murabitun.
rows.anchor: Istılâh-ı fukahâda murâbıt süğūrdan birine bir müddet beklemek için gidendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In contemporary terminology a murabit is a soldier under arms, stationed in barracks or outposts and taking guard duty.
rows.anchor: Zamanımız ıstılâhına göre murâbıt fî sebîlillâh silah altında bulunan ve kışla ve karakollarda duran ve nevbet bekleyen askerler demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim from Sahl b. Saʿd says one day of border guard duty in God’s path is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: Buhârî ve Müslim’de Sehl b. Sa‘d’dan rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound-chain report in Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayra says one who dies guarding the border in God’s path continues to receive the reward and provision of righteous work, is safe from the tester, and is raised safe from terror.
rows.anchor: İbn Mâce’de sened-i sahîh ile Ebû Hureyre’den mervî olan bir hadîs-i şerîfte de Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abu al-Shaykh from Anas as a Prophetic report says prayer in a border station is worth two million prayers.
rows.anchor: Ebu’ş-Şeyh’in Hazret-i Enes’ten merfû‘an tahrîc ettiği bir hadiste

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says ribat is superior to jihad because it protects Muslim lives, whereas jihad sheds the blood of polytheists.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâdan mervîdir ki “ribât, cihaddan efdaldir. Zira ribât Müslümanların kanını muhafazadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety leads to success, fulfilled aspirations, and answered prayers; the ending prayer of al-Baqara is answered in this way.
rows.anchor: İşte Sûre-i Bakara nihâyetindeki فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ duasının da tam cevâbı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran closes at a meeting point with al-Baqara; al-Nisa begins as a further unfolding of divine upbringing, human creation and brotherhood, family rights and duties, and religious education.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Âl-i İmrân hitâm bularak Zehrâveyn bir nokta-i visâlde telâkī eylemiş ve bunun bir inkişâf-ı mahsûsu olmak üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poor guardian or trustee may take a fair amount for the work and service performed and necessary needs; a wealthy one should abstain.
rows.anchor: fakir olan velî veya vasî de mâruf vechile ücret-i sa‘y ü hizmeti ve hâcet-i zarûriyesi kadar yesin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of fair dealing is clarified by prohibitions on consuming wealth wrongfully or unjustly, including the orphan’s property, and by the command to uphold justice for orphans.
rows.anchor: Bu mâruf لَا تَأْكُلُوٓا۟ أَمْوَٰلَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ [el-Bakara 2/188; en-Nisâ 4/29], إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ ظُلْمًا [en-Nisâ 4/10], وَأَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلْيَتَٰمَىٰ بِٱلْقِسْطِ [en-Nisâ 4/127] âyetleriyle mâlum olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When handing orphans their property, the guardian should deliver it in the presence of witnesses.
rows.anchor: O yetimlerin mallarını kendilerine teslim ettiğiniz zaman da onlara karşı şâhid tutunuz, şâhid huzurunda veriniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sufficient as accountant: obedience means no other accountant need be feared, and disobedience cannot be rescued by another accountant.
rows.anchor: Allah da bütün hesaplarınızı görmeye kâfidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed after Rifaʿa died leaving his young son Sabit and the boy’s guardian asked the Prophet what share of the property he could lawfully use and when he should return it.
rows.anchor: Rifâ‘a vefat etmiş ve oğlu Sâbit’i sağīr olarak bırakmış idi, velîsi “taht-ı hıcrimde biraderzâdem var, bunun malından bana ne kadar helâl olur ve malını ne zaman teslim edeyim?” diye Resûlullah’a sormuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion now moves on to inheritance rulings.
rows.anchor: Şimdi de miras ahkâmına geçiliyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents prevent people from the Qur’an, the Prophet, and belief in truth, while distancing themselves from it and unwittingly destroying only themselves.
rows.anchor: hem de kendileri uzak kaçarlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers will be held at the Fire and wish they had been returned so they would not deny God’s signs and could be believers; the outcome is dreadful.
rows.anchor: bu kâfirlerin, mükezziblerin ateşe tutuldukları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wish concerns the signs and indications that warned of events and consequences before they occurred.
rows.anchor: Rabbimizin âyetlerini, vâkı‘âtı ve âkıbetleri vukū‘undan evvel ihbar eden delâil ve işârâtını tekzib etmese idik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who first denied truth and followed the wrong path end in the Fire, recognize the punishment for their errors, and then desperately wish to return and follow the right path.
rows.anchor: İbtidâ hakkı inkâr ve tekzib edenler, yanlış yola gidenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their regret is not sincere faith: the evil, hypocrisy, and corrupt deeds they had concealed are exposed to them, and they recoil from that exposure.
rows.anchor: Hayır, bundan evvel gizledikleri fenalıklar, nifakları, a‘mâl-i habîseleri karşılarına çıkar, yüzlerine vurulur da bu ondandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If returned to worldly life, they would repeat the forbidden behavior; their promise is a lie, as they had repeatedly shown regret in worldly crises and then resumed their conduct.
rows.anchor: Dünyada böyle kaç defalar başları sıkılmış, nedametler göstermişlerdir de ilk fırsatta yine eski yaptıklarını yapmışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even after seeing the afterlife, they would again claim that only worldly life exists and deny resurrection, because unbelief and sin have become settled habits.
rows.anchor: Küfr ü me‘âsî bunlara bu kadar müstakir bir huy olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their unbelief and sins are so entrenched that they neither can nor will return to the right path.
rows.anchor: Bunun için ne dönebilirler ne döndürülürler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Lord’s presence they will acknowledge that resurrection is true, swearing by their Lord, and God will tell them to taste the punishment for their former disbelief.
rows.anchor: “evet yâ Rabbi, hak imiş, Rabbimize kasem olsun ki hak imiş” diyecekler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny meeting God remain in loss until the Hour overtakes them suddenly; they lament their neglect while bearing their burdens on their backs, a terrible load.
rows.anchor: Tâ vakt ü sâat kendilerine ansızın gelinceye kadar inkâr ettiler de o vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers of resurrection and the Judgment have two further states: loss and the carrying of great burdens and sins.
rows.anchor: Bu âyette ba‘s ü kıyameti inkâr edenlerin diğer bir hâlleri îzah olunmuştur ki birisi hüsran, birisi de büyük vizirler, veballer çekmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusran is losing sight of immense reward and lasting bliss; vizr or wabal means being caught within immense punishment.
rows.anchor: “Hüsran” sevâb-ı azîmin, na‘îm-i mukīmin fevt ü zayâ‘ını görmek, “vizr” ü “vebal” de ikāb-ı azîmin içinde kalmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed the sacred rational soul in the bodily world and gave it physical faculties and reason to acquire true knowledge and virtuous morals whose benefits appear after death.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ nefs-i nâtıka-i kudsiye cevherini bu âlem-i cismânîye sevk buyurmuş ve ona şu gördüğümüz âlât-ı cismâniye ve edevât-ı cesedâniyeyi vermiş ve akl ü tefekkür ihsan etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using one’s faculties and reason to pursue limited, dangerous pleasures and transient happiness produces irreparable loss at life’s end: both capital and supposed profit perish.
rows.anchor: insan bu âlât ü edevâtı, bu kuvve-i akliye ve fikriyesini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even someone who welcomes death as release from life’s pains must face this loss and leave the world in enduring sorrow and longing.
rows.anchor: onun için bu hüsrânı görmek ve bunun âlâm-ı dilsûzuyla gözlerini kapayıp en büyük lezzet bildiği bu âleme ebedî bir ye’s-i hazîn içinde hasretle veda edip gitmek muhakkaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This loss and regret belong to those who deny resurrection and treat immediate worldly pleasures as the ultimate happiness and perfection.
rows.anchor: bu hüsrân ü hasret ve bu elem-i müebbed, ba‘s ü kıyâmeti inkâr eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who prepare for the Hereafter depart like a lover summoned toward the beloved place of the heart.
rows.anchor: o dem-i firakta hicrân-ı gurbetten ma‘şûk-ı vicdânı olan semt-i cânâna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿa ordinarily means a small unit of time, one twenty-fourth of day and night; with the article it names the Day of Judgment and accountability, possibly because its accounting is swift.
rows.anchor: “Sâ‘at”, eczâ-yı zamandan bir cüz’-i kalîlin ismidir ki gece ile gündüzün yirmi dört cüz’de bir cüz’üdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes al-Saʿa to mean the moment the Resurrection begins, named for its sudden arrival at an hour known only to God.
rows.anchor: İkinci bir kavle göre de kıyâmetin koptuğu vaktin ismidir ki Allah’tan başka kimsenin bilmediği bir saatte ansızın bastıracağından dolayı tesmiye edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is also called a kind of resurrection because it begins the transition to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: vakt-i mevt de âhirete intikalin bir başlangıcı ve mukaddimesi olmak itibariyle mevt de kıyamet cinsinden addedilip o nâm ile yâd olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life considered by itself is only heedlessness and a useless game; anyone who reflects on its passing pleasures while remembering death will see this.
rows.anchor: hayât-ı dünyâ mücerred hayât-ı dünya olmak itibariyle lehv ü la‘bden başka bir şey değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say worldly life is all there is seek amusement and games to forget life’s end.
rows.anchor: en büyük zevki onu ve âkıbetini unutmak için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads the phrase as waladāru al-ākhira rather than walildāru al-ākhira.
rows.anchor: -İbn ‘Âmir وَلَدَارُ الاْٰخِرَةِ-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is better for the Godfearing because its life lasts and its benefits and pleasures are pure and enduring; piety means guarding against unbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: ve herhâlde dâr-ı uhrâ, âhiret evi, son vatan, hayât-ı âhire evi, lehv ü la‘ibden küfr ü me‘âsîden korunur olan müttakīler hakkında hayırlıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He addresses people rhetorically, asking whether they will reason about worldly life and cling to piety.
rows.anchor: ey insanlar akıl etmez misiniz, aklınız yok mu ki hayât-ı dünyânın ne olduğunu düşünüp de takvâya sarılasınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Shuʿba from Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf al-Ashir read “do they not reason?” in place of “do you not reason?”
rows.anchor: İbn Kesir, Ebû Amr ve Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be, Hamza, Kisâî, Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde اَفَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ okunduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the rebuke is directed at deniers of resurrection who have no reason to be so heedless, chase distractions, deny God, the Prophet, and the Hereafter, and ignore piety.
rows.anchor: ba‘s ü sa‘ati inkâr edenlerin hiç aklı yok mu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns to console and strengthen the Prophet against the disbelievers’ denial and mockery.
rows.anchor: Küffârın tekzîb ü şemâtetlerine karşı Resûlullah’ı tesliye ve takviye için buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Abraham not only the stars, moon, and sun but the whole cosmos as a dominion under rule, disclosing the mysteries and laws of divine lordship to his heart.
rows.anchor: gökleri ve Yer’i gözüne gösterdikten başka

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham perceived one unique divine power gathering and governing the material and spiritual worlds; a human creature has honor above the stars, so serving another creature beneath the true sovereign is grave error and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: bütün bu âlemleri toplayıp nefs-i İbrâhim’e indiren ve maddiyat ve mâneviyâtıyla ona rabt edip hepsini birden idare ve tedbir eden kudret-i rabbâniye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Abraham this dominion so that he would become one of those possessing certainty.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim’e bu melekûtu gösteriyorduk ki öyle desin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s words “this is my Lord” on seeing a star first serve as a taunt to those around him, questioning whether a star could nurture a human being.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ bir yıldızın bir insanı terbiye edebileceğini istib‘âd ederek etrafındakilere bir târiz yaptı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying he does not love those that set, Abraham teaches that love grounds lordship and worship, while motion and setting show createdness, subjection, change, and perishability; the true Lord creates, acts, and is free from extinction.
rows.anchor: rubûbiyet ve ubûdiyette mahabbetin üssü’l-esâs olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument about setting also exposes the contradiction of replacing setting stars with idols: if the original star is inadequate, its fashioned image is even less worthy.
rows.anchor: ufûllerinden dolayı asıllarının kâfi olmadığını teslim ettikleri hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham repeats the same argumentative taunt when the moon rises, then says he would be among the misguided if his Lord did not guide him, confessing dependence on divine guidance and gratitude for it.
rows.anchor: hem de her lahza rabbine olan ihtiyâcını itiraf ile hidâyetine şükretmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statements “this is my Lord” are argumentative and ironic, not sincere affirmation; without a moment of divine guidance, humanity could mistake a transient object for the everlasting and fall into error.
rows.anchor: هَٰذَا رَبِّى sözlerinin iltizâmî olmayıp ilzâmî ve inkârî olduğunu anlatmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon’s beauty can readily captivate people; without God’s instant guidance, humanity in darkness would worship the moon, stars, or idols.
rows.anchor: zulmetteki beşeriyet Ay’a da tapacak, yıldıza da tapacak, puta da tapacak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the sun appears Abraham makes the same taunt more forcefully, calling it the greatest of the objects presented as a lord.
rows.anchor: “Bu benim rabbim ha! Bu hepsinden büyük!” dedi. Ve daha büyük bir târiz yaptı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the sun sets, Abraham declares himself free of the things his people associate with God and turns wholly, as a pure monotheist, to the Creator of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: Ben Hanîf, tertemiz bir muvahhid olarak bütün mevcûdiyetimle yüzümü cemî‘-i muhteveyâtıyla şu semâvât ve arzı yaratan Zât-ı ecell ü a‘lâ’ya tevcih ettim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham affirms that from beginning to end he never compromised with polytheists, proclaiming certainty in divine unity and establishing his hanif identity.
rows.anchor: tevhîde îkānını ilan ve hanîfiyeti isbat ve takrir eyledi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people challenge and threaten him, seeking to win the argument; he dismisses their verbal and practical dispute and intimidation, then argues from love and fear to establish lordship and worship.
rows.anchor: Kavmi de kendisine karşı mücadele ve tahvif ile hüccet yarışına kalkıştılar, galebe fikrine düştüler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham begins his reply by asking whether they dispute with him about God when He has already guided him.
rows.anchor: أَتُحَٰٓجُّونِّى فِى ٱللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَىٰنِ
